findings.question: C13
findings.title: Casing bevels need face-weighted normals; the 40 degree split alone will bend the flat faces
findings.recommendation: The v03 builder writes custom normals so that every flat casing face keeps its own face normal at the vertices it shares with a bevel, and the turn happens only across the bevel faces. S measures it on the export: on every casing triangle larger than 4 cm2, each exported vertex normal is within 2 degrees of the triangle normal.
findings.rationale: The frozen builder marks every face smooth, splits edges only above 40 degrees and writes no custom normals. A two-segment bevel has 30 degree steps, so each flat face joins the same smooth group as the bevel beside it and its corner normals tilt. A large flat face then shades as a soft dome. The art direction asked for weighted normals for this reason.
findings.evidence: sourceDerived for the builder behaviour; the size of the visible effect is futureRendered
findings.missingEvidence: Actual music-1440 and right-down images of the white controller shell with bevels; exported-normal deviation per row

findings.question: C2 and C11
findings.title: One stool foot already floats beyond the rug; placement D makes it worse and the proposed +0.04 shift does not fix it
findings.recommendation: Add a contact rule to the combined check: every foot of a supported object rests on one surface, either all inside the rug flat field or all on the bare floor at floor height, with at least 20 mm between any foot and the binding. The author chooses the stool position and leg rotation that meets it and re-measures occlusion.
findings.rationale: The helper places stool feet at rug height without testing the rug outline. In the frozen v02 geometry one foot sits 63 to 94 mm beyond the rug front edge with its underside 8.6 mm above the bare floor. Under D the seat centre lands on the rug edge. With the proposed +0.04 shift one foot is still 130 to 161 mm off the rug and one straddles the edge. Sliding the stool toward the keyboard needs +0.26 to get all feet inside the outline and +0.30 to clear the binding, which pushes the stool into the stand footprint.
findings.missingEvidence: Combined CPU measurement with the chosen stool position; right-down-1440 and phone right-down images showing stool feet and rug front edge

findings.question: C13
findings.title: Keys cannot be exempted wholesale; the white-key front lip needs authored shape and fits the row ceiling
findings.recommendation: Remove keys from the blanket variance. Author one edge treatment on the front top edge of each white key, exaggerated to about 3 mm or more so it is over one pixel at music-1440. All other key edges may stay sharp. Other listed hand-scale parts may stay sharp for this candidate, each named, with the invalidation conditions under c13Classes.
findings.rationale: Key fronts are the named identifying feature of the keys row and root asked to preserve them. The plan rejects key bevels because a full bevel on 49 keys exceeds the ceiling. A front-lip-only treatment costs about 4 triangles per white key with one segment or 8 with two: 1052 or 1168 of 1540. The detail floor says small features are omitted or exaggerated; it does not say an identifying edge is dropped.
findings.evidence: triangle arithmetic is my estimate; the builder must assert exact counts
findings.missingEvidence: Actual music-1440 crop of the key row; phone music crop; exact counts

findings.question: C2
findings.title: The 0.36 degree azimuth margin equals about 24 mm of sideways placement; yaw can widen it
findings.recommendation: Pin the visible-sample method and measure the built candidate with it. Treat the margin as a measurement risk. The author may test a little more yaw toward the eye and a stand height nearer the lower gate bound.
findings.rationale: My unoccluded envelope gives 32.14 degrees at base and 31.53 at D, a constant 1.17 degrees above the author figures, with the same differences between variants. authoringAmendmentConditions: Scope: full-kit stages M3 and M4 authored by build scripts. It replaces only the live-modifier clauses at art-direction.md:129 and :144 and technical-plan.md:54 for those stages.

Master: the hash-pinned build script and geometry helper are the editable master. The saved Blender file is a snapshot. A re-run from the pinned inputs reproduces each row with the same triangle count and bounds.
One bevel table: class to radius after tier factor and segment count, in one named place in the helper, used by bevel-aware primitives. No literal bevel sizes at call sites.
Declared edges: each bevelled edge set and each sharp exemption is declared in source with a reason: contact face, screen face, or a named variance.
Normals: the builder writes face-weighted custom normals in place of the Weighted Normal modifier (finding N1).
Receipts: per row, the builder records triangles, bevelled edge length by class, and remaining hard edge length by reason.

Not waived: versioned stage files never overwritten, build script kept with the stage, library materials linked, the row and reuse contract. A hand edit to a saved Blender file, or a bevel-class change at M6 without re-running the builders, voids the amendment for that stage.

threejs-geometry.applies: Normals drive lighting (its vertex-attribute section). Supports N1: shading follows the exported NORMAL attribute, so the normals must be authored.
threejs-geometry.conflicts: Runtime ExtrudeGeometry bevels, merging and instancing conflict with the frozen named-leaf and draw contracts. Not adopted.

threejs-materials.applies: Roughness and environment response decide whether an edge highlight shows. With no environment map, bevels on black parts show little; this supports the C13 priority order.
threejs-materials.conflicts: Any material or environment-map change conflicts with the frozen library. None proposed.

threejs-lighting.applies: Shadow bias guidance: a normalBias of the order it suggests is larger than the 8 mm rug and the 8.6 mm float, so the shadow pass will not reliably hide or reveal the floating foot. Contact must be right in geometry.
threejs-lighting.conflicts: Its fake contact-shadow recipes conflict with the imported-decal contract. Runtime-owned; no change requested.

webgl-landing-steering.applies: Only its principle that readability comes before added detail, which supports spending triangles on the key lip and white shell first.
webgl-landing-steering.conflicts: Its lanes with orbit cameras, post-processing and compression conflict with the fixed-eye, demand-render and dependency contracts. Not adopted.
